title: Prompt Architect — Smokestack Iterations
content:
Quick context:
- Personal scratchpad for the 'smokestack' prompt family — trying to build compact templates that survive: (a) length-constrained contexts (<= 512 tokens), (b) adversarial user edits, and (c) multi-turn memory noise.
- Goal: library of ~10 resilient templates + canonical few-shot packs for structured tasks (summary, instruction, extraction).
- Notes to self: keep examples short, prefer explicit labels (INPUT / RULES / OUTPUT) rather than verbose instructions.

Observations so far (raw):
- Model drifts on vague role descriptors. 'You are a helpful assistant' alone is weak. Adding a single sentence of constraints (max bullets, format) increases stability.
- Few-shot exemplars that mix styles confuse the model more than they help; keep exemplars stylistically consistent with target output.
- When users append contradictory instructions mid-conversation, prefer authoritative last-turn cues: e.g., 'Ignore previous constraints except the one labeled FINAL'.

Working template candidates (short):
1) Extraction-minimal (for structured key-value pulls)
Template: "TASK: Extract exact key-value pairs. INPUT: <user_text>. RULES: return JSON with keys [name, date, amount]. If missing, use null. OUTPUT:"
Example few-shot (2 shots):
- IN: "Invoice: Acme Co, 2024-08-01, $12,000. Customer: Jane Doe"
  OUT: {"name": "Acme Co", "date": "2024-08-01", "amount": "12000"}
- IN: "Receipt: FooBar LLC 2025-02-10 $350"
  OUT: {"name": "FooBar LLC", "date": "2025-02-10", "amount": "350"}
Notes: include numeric normalization step in RULES for amounts.

2) Short-form summary (user wants 1-2 sentence TL;DR)
Template: "TASK: TL;DR in 1-2 sentences. CONTEXT: <text>. CONSTRAINTS: max 30 words, avoid jargon, preserve sentiment. OUTPUT:"
Few-shot: two balanced examples (long doc -> 1 sentence).
Failure modes observed: when original text has ambiguity, model hallucinates specific claims. Mitigation: add RULES: 'If not explicit, say "ambiguous" or "not specified".'

3) Instruction-clarify flow (for instruction-following UIs)
Template: "You are an assistant that rewrites unclear user goals into step-by-step tasks. INPUT GOAL: <user_goal>. RULES: produce 3 numbered steps, each 1 line, and a single-line acceptance criteria. OUTPUT:"
Few-shot: use 3-shot to show long->concise conversion.

Failure case catalogue (recent):
- CASE A: Partial token truncation. Example: user paste >512 tokens, model completes but drops last item in list. Quick patch: preface with 'If input truncated, respond: "INPUT_TRUNCATED" and list what is missing.'
- CASE B: Adversarial punctuation: extra backticks or unbalanced brackets cause JSON extraction to break. Patch: RULES: 'Sanitize input: remove unmatched `, \`, and stray opening brackets before extraction.'
- CASE C: Conflicting user edits mid-turn. Example: user: 'Do X' then 'Actually do Y' within same turn. Model sometimes blends. Strategy: emphasize 'use the last instruction labeled FINAL' pattern.

Experiment matrix (next runs):
- A/B: exemplar count (0 / 2 / 5) x explicit-normalization (on/off) x style-consistency (mixed/consistent). Metrics: output match rate on ground-truth set, token-efficiency, hallucination rate (binary).
- Stress test: random injected garbage tokens (5% token noise) across input, measure extraction robustness.

Mini checklist before claiming a template stable:
- [ ] Survives truncation heuristic (detects and returns INPUT_TRUNCATED when needed)
- [ ] No structural hallucinations across 100 validation samples
- [ ] Keeps outputs within token budget for target use-case
- [ ] Matches canonical format >95% on gold set

Scratchy prompt variants (short form, try in console):
- Variant 1: add 'STRICT_JSON: true' line to encourage JSON only responses.
- Variant 2: append 'EXPLAIN: No' to avoid chain-of-thought. Watch for refusal-like terse outputs.
- Variant 3: preface with a single-line persona: 'Assistant is a minimal data-extractor that never adds fields.'

Notes on few-shot exemplar selection (heuristic):
- Prefer positive examples and 1 negative example demonstrating a common mistake (then RULES: 'avoid this mistake').
- Keep labels explicit: INPUT / EXPECTED / WHY (brief). The WHY helps regularize but increases prompt length. Evaluate tradeoff.

To-dos (short-term):
- [ ] Create 100 synthetic extraction test cases (edge cases: nested dates, currencies w/ commas, ambiguous names). (assigned to Ethan)
- [ ] Run A/B with STRICT_JSON toggle across 3 model sizes (S, M, L) and record hallucination rate (me).
- [ ] Draft a confluence summary once one template hits >90% on gold.

Loose ideas / future experiments (brain dump):
- Token-level prefix caching for repeated templates: precompile RULES as a cacheable prefix to save prompt tokens in hosted flow. Talk to SDK folks.
- Meta-example selection: runtime choose which exemplar to include based on input similarity. Needs lightweight embedding search; maybe use local KNN on a tiny vector store.
- Small-controller pattern: two-step prompt where step 1 validates input shape, step 2 does extraction. Should reduce hallucination but doubles cost. Benchmark.

Random scrap notes to remember:
- I liked the 'label-last' trick we tried in September; revisit how often it helps versus confusing multi-turn.
- Keep a short 'counterexample' repository: one-line examples of how not to prompt for each template.

References / links (quick):
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROMPT/Smokestack+Index
- GH PR with lightweight eval harness: https://github.com/redwood/rl-infra/pull/891
- Ticket for hallucination baseline: JIRA RL-5423

End of scratchpad.

-- Marisol
